correctness.rationale: Solving the exact two-step Lion recurrence yields the unique momentum pair for any candidate phase \(a\). The two strict sign inequalities reduce exactly to \(\beta_1\eta/(1+\beta_2)<a<\eta[1-\beta_1/(1+\beta_2)]\), which is nonempty exactly when \(2\beta_1<1+\beta_2\). The fixed-sign two-step derivative has eigenvalues \(1\) and \(\beta_2^2\), and direct completion of the square gives the exact average-loss floor.

value.rationale: Lion's fixed-magnitude sign update and asymmetric two-coefficient momentum are its defining algorithmic features. The theorem shows exactly how those features create a nonzero terminal chattering set even on the simplest strongly convex objective, quantifies when the set exists, its transverse contraction, its width at the published defaults, and the irreducible constant-step loss floor. This is a natural dynamical invariant that directly informs learning-rate decay and terminal-accuracy behavior.
